standard.title: Specification for Sounding Pipes

sectional_committee.name: Marine Engineering and Shipbuilding Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the material quality, dimensions, tolerances, and design requirements for various sounding pipes and associated fittings installed on board ships to measure and assess the liquid levels of double bottom tanks, deep tanks, and bilges.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the material quality, dimensions, tolerances, and design requirements for various sounding pipes and associated fittings installed on board ships to measure and assess the liquid levels of double bottom tanks, deep tanks, and bilges.

certification.description: Voluntary Engineering Design and Material Standard. Since IS 4010 is an outfitting design standard rather than a safety-critical consumer product, it is certified on a voluntary basis. Manufacturers are eligible to apply for a BIS license to use the Standard Mark (ISI Certification Mark). However, compliance with its dimensional, material, and installation requirements is universally mandated inside all national public, defense, Indian Navy, port authority, and commercial shipyard procurement contracts to ensure seamless compatibility and leak-proof safety of marine tanks.
requirements: Products conforming to the requirements may be legibly marked with the ISI Certification Mark as a safeguard of quality compliance.

All sounding pipes must be made of heavy quality steel tubes per IS:1239-1964 and coated with a protective material. For pipes not in contact with fuel or cargo oil, hot-dip galvanizing is permitted on completion.
The self-closing cock with a parallel plug fitted to the head of the sounding pipe must be manufactured from brass or closed grain cast iron.
Fittings to the head of the sounding pipe placed on decks must be flush deck fittings equipped with a hinged cover pilfer-proof cap to prevent damage, water entry, and unauthorized access.

Sounding pipe heads in way of the bulkhead deck and machinery spaces must follow standard dimensions in Table 1 across nominal bores of 32, 40, 50, and 65 mm. The height of sounding pipes above the deck must depend on the surrounding compartment space.
Details of attachments in way of intermediate decks are specified as Type A (sleeve with lock nut) and Type B (flanged), with dimensions specified in Table 2.

Sounding pipe attachments in way of a deck or tank top are specified as Type A (sleeve and screwed flanges) and Type B (flanges with a strengthening plate). Type B includes a requirement for drilling 12 mm air release holes.

To prevent the heavy sounding rod from puncturing or damaging the ship's bottom plating under repeated drops, a striker plate (or a guide equipped with a striker plate) must be provided at the bottom of the sounding pipe, welded directly to the pipe or positioned on the tank bottom plate or keel.

Sounding pipes must be installed in all cargo spaces, fuel oil tanks, structural ship tanks, and watertight compartments. Openings must prevent free water entry. Pipes in cargo spaces must be protected (with steel protection in coal bunkers), and soundings must be taken as near the suction pipes as practicable.
